newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo Dec retail sales up but below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo Dec retail sales up but below forecasts.

text.p: Retail sales in the city of Sao Paulo rose sharply in December over the same month of 1995, but failed to meet expectations of retailers of a surge in sales due to the Christmas season, the Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP) said.

Credit sales climbed 27.6 percent last month over the same period of 1995, below expectations of a rise of 40 percent, while cash sales rose only 3.8 percent, against estimates of between 8.0 percent and 10 percent, said Emilio Alfieri, an economist at the ACSP.
Alfieri said the weaker-than-expected figures show that consumers preferred to pay off debts or save money at year's end.

"Customers are very cautious, seeking not to spend too much money and accumulate debts," he said, adding that consumer and retailer caution mounted after consumer defaults reached high levels in the past two years.

As Christmas sales were lower than expected, Sao Paulo's retailers are beginning 1997 with stocks, encouraging them to offer goods at a discount and contributing to slow down the economy in the first quarter, Alfieri said.
